### AI readiness test in 10 questions and 3 minutes, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-readiness

An AI readiness test for small business owners and team leaders. Ten questions score your team out of 30 and give you three next steps. No email required.

**What the test measures** Ten questions about how your team works today: how you write to customers, how recently you adopted a tool that saved time, how much admin work repeats every week, how new staff learn the job, how you use data, how you produce marketing, and how you and your team think about AI.

**What you get back** A score out of 30, one of four levels, and three next steps in the order to do them. The test runs in your browser, takes three minutes, and asks for no email.

**Who built it** I am Elijah Purcell, Founder/CEO of Purcell Ventures LLC in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and I wrote this test. Each answer scores 0 to 3 points, for a total out of 30, and the total places you in one of four tiers. The point values come from running COSMIC, a station of 57 AI agents in 17 rooms that does my company's proposals, site audits and security checks.

### AI cost calculator, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-cost-calculator

A free calculator by Elijah Purcell. It takes team size, hourly cost and manual workload, and shows how fast an AI consulting session pays back in dollars and hours.

**Start from a preset** Each preset fills in the inputs for a typical business of that kind.

**Your inputs** The number of people whose work you want to speed up.

**Your estimated savings** At those inputs, the session pays back in 3 days. After that, the savings continue each month.

**How the math works** You enter team size, a loaded hourly rate, and how many hours a week go into repetitive written work: drafting, replying, summarising and formatting. The calculator multiplies those hours by the automation share you pick, compares the savings with the cost of a session, and gives you the payback period.

**When to skip the session** If your team is small and the repetitive writing takes a couple of hours a week, the payback period will be long and you should skip the session. The calculator shows that result too.

**A session built on your own workflows** I come to your office, work from your own workflows, and build at least one automation with you during the session. I reply within one business day.

### AI consulting in Alabama, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-consulting

AI consulting in Alabama from Elijah Purcell in Tuscaloosa: AI, automation and custom software for local businesses. Prices and when AI is the wrong buy.

**What does an AI consultant do for an Alabama business?** An AI consultant looks at the work your business repeats every week and sorts it into three piles: work an AI tool or automation can take over, work that needs custom software, and work that should stay with a person. Then the consultant trains your team or builds the system.

**How much does AI consulting cost?** At Purcell Ventures, a 1-on-1 session costs $175 an hour, small group training costs $125 a person, and a half-day workshop costs $2,500 flat for up to 20 people. Small software projects run $1,500 to $3,500. I quote automation work per project after a free conversation, because the price depends on how many systems it touches.

**Is my business ready for AI consulting?** Most businesses are ready if they have work that repeats, information already kept in some digital tool, and one person who will own the change. You do not need technical staff. The AI readiness test scores your team out of 30 in 10 questions, takes about three minutes and asks for no email.

**Do I need training, automation or custom software?** Training fits when your team already has the right software and needs to use AI tools well. Automation fits when a task repeats on a schedule and follows the same steps each time. Custom software fits when the tool you need does not exist, or the version you can buy forces your team to work around it.

**How does a consulting project with Purcell Ventures work?** It starts with a free conversation by phone or email about what your team spends its time on. If AI or software fits, I propose a session or quote a build. If it does not fit, I tell you on that first call.

**Do you work with businesses outside Tuscaloosa?** Yes. I work with businesses across Alabama and do digital work for businesses anywhere in the US. Training sessions run at your location, and planning and builds work over phone and email. Owners in Birmingham, Huntsville, Montgomery, Mobile and Auburn start the same way, with a free call.

**When is AI consulting the wrong purchase?** AI consulting is the wrong purchase when the real problem is a broken process, missing records or software your team owns and never set up. It is also the wrong purchase when a free tool already covers the need. In those cases I say so and point you to the cheaper fix.

**Who runs Purcell Ventures?** Purcell Ventures LLC is a one-person company run by me, Elijah Purcell, a student in New College and the Honors College at the University of Alabama. The person you meet with is the person who writes the code and answers your email.

## Topic guides

### Autonomous AI agent systems, by Elijah Purcell
URL: https://purcellventures.co/agentic-ai

What an autonomous AI agent system is, how it differs from a chatbot or a workflow, and what it takes to run COSMIC, 57 AI agents in 17 rooms, in production.

**What an agent system is** An autonomous AI agent system is one where a model decides what to do next on its own. A workflow runs steps in a fixed order, and a chatbot answers when someone messages it. An agent gets a goal, a set of tools and a boundary, and picks its own sequence. Most of the engineering goes into the constraints around the model.

**Production failures** Four things that broke in COSMIC, and how I fixed each one.

**Common questions** Written by Elijah Purcell , Founder/CEO of Purcell Ventures LLC, from a system that has run daily since 2026. Related: the COSMIC agent roster and What the agents get wrong .

**Agent systems for your business** I scope custom software and AI automation on a free 30-minute discovery call. I reply within one business day.

### AI in design for small businesses, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-design

AI in design for small businesses: what AI tools do well and badly for logos, brand identity, websites and social graphics, and when to hire a designer instead.

**What can AI design tools do for a small business?** AI design tools are good at first drafts and variations: color palettes, font pairings, layout options, social post templates and background images. They are weak at anything that has to be exact, original or legally yours, such as a logo, lettering inside an image, or a brand that has to look the same everywhere it appears.

**Can I use an AI-generated logo for my business?** You can, with three problems to plan for. Image generators produce pixel images, while a logo needs a vector file that scales from a business card to a sign. AI images often garble letters. And the US Copyright Office has said it will not register material that an AI generated without human creative control.

**Can AI build a brand identity?** AI can draft the pieces of a brand identity: a palette with hex codes, a font pairing, notes on voice and a draft tagline. It cannot tell what sets your business apart from the shop down the street, and it does not keep those pieces consistent across your sign, website, truck and menu. A person has to write the rules down and check them.

**Can AI design my business website?** AI website builders can produce a working layout from a short description, and that is a reasonable start for a simple site. The weak spots are the parts that bring in customers: accurate copy about your services, photos of your real work, fast loading on a phone, accessibility, and structured information that search engines and AI answer engines can read.

**Is AI good for social media graphics?** Social graphics are the best fit for AI design tools. Businesses post often, posts live for a short time and get a glance in a feed, so speed counts for more than originality. The way to keep them on brand is to start each post from a template in your own colors and logo and let AI fill in the image and caption.

**Where does AI fall short in design?** AI falls short wherever the result has to be exact, lasting or provably yours. Logos and photos of real work sit at that end, and social graphics and palettes sit at the other.

**When should a small business hire a designer?** Hire a designer for anything you will use for years or print in large numbers: the logo, signs, vehicle graphics, packaging and the core brand guide. Use AI for work you make often and replace quickly, such as social posts, flyers for one event and draft layouts. Mistakes in the long-lived pieces cost the most to undo.

**How does Purcell Ventures use AI in its own design work?** The design tools I built put AI at the drafting stage and leave the final file to a person. The logo concept generator writes directions instead of drawing a finished logo. The brand kit builder drafts a palette, fonts and voice notes for a person to approve. The social templates tool writes formats with blanks for the business to fill.

### AI automation for small businesses, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-automation

AI automation for small businesses: which tasks to automate first, what AI phone answering and booking can do, what to keep with a person, and what it costs.

**What is AI automation, and how is it different from regular automation?** Regular automation moves information along fixed rules: when a form arrives, add a row to a sheet and send an email. AI automation adds a language model to one or more steps, so the system can read a message, sort it, draft a reply or pull details out of a document. The rules still decide what happens next.

**Which task should a small business automate first?** Automate first the task that happens most often, follows the same steps each time, and causes harm when someone forgets it. For most service businesses that is follow-up: replying to new leads, chasing quotes that went quiet, and reminding customers about invoices and appointments.

**Can AI answer the phone and book appointments?** Yes, for routine calls. AI voice tools can answer, give hours and prices, take a message and book into a connected calendar. They handle a caller with an unusual problem poorly, and an upset caller worse. Set one up with a script, a short list of questions it may answer, and a transfer to a person for everything else.

**How do I automate follow-ups with leads and unpaid invoices?** Send every new lead an immediate reply and a notice to the owner, then schedule follow-ups on fixed days until the lead answers. Most invoicing tools, including QuickBooks and Stripe, can send payment reminders on a schedule once you switch the feature on. The setup takes an afternoon.

**Can I automate asking customers for Google reviews?** Yes. Send every customer the same review request a day or two after the job, with a direct link to your Google review form. Ask every customer. Google's review policies prohibit asking only the customers you expect to be happy, a practice called review gating.

**Should I use Zapier or Make, or pay for a custom automation?** Use Zapier or Make when both apps appear on their connection lists and the task has a handful of steps. Pay for a custom automation when the data needs cleaning first, the task needs a model to read or write text, or the monthly task count costs more than a one-time build.

**What should a business never hand to an AI automation?** Keep with a person anything that moves money, makes a legal or medical promise, refuses a customer, or speaks for the business in a dispute. An automation can draft those messages and queue them, and a person should send them.

**What happens when an automation breaks?** Most automations fail without an error message. A login expires or a form field changes name, and the task stops while every dashboard still looks normal. The fix is a check that compares what the automation did against what it should have done, sent to a person who reads it.

### AI integration for small business software, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-integration

AI integration for small business: connect AI to Google Workspace, QuickBooks, a CRM, your website, phone and text. Off-the-shelf vs custom, safety, prices.

**What does it mean to integrate AI into software I already use?** Integrating AI means a model reads from or writes to a system you already run, so nobody has to copy text into a chat window and paste the answer back. The model might sort incoming email, summarize a customer record, draft a quote from a form or answer questions on your website from your own documents.

**How does AI connect to Google Workspace, QuickBooks and a CRM?** Start with the AI features each product already includes, because they come with the vendor's data terms and need no setup. Google builds Gemini into Gmail, Docs and Sheets on business plans. Intuit has added AI features to QuickBooks. Most CRMs offer AI summaries and email drafts, often on their higher plans.

**Should I buy an AI tool off the shelf or build something custom?** Buy off the shelf when a product does the whole job and your data fits its format. Build custom when the job spans systems no product connects, when the paid tier you need costs more each year than a one-time build, or when the tool forces your team to keep a spreadsheet on the side.

**How do I put AI on my website and phone line?** On a website, the common integration is a chatbot that answers from your own services, prices, hours and policies, with a handoff to a person when it does not know. On the phone, it is an AI voice tool that answers routine calls, or a text service that replies to missed calls and booking requests.

**How do I get an AI to answer from my own business documents?** Give the model your documents at the moment it answers, and tell it to answer only from them. Developers call this retrieval: the system finds the passages that match the question and hands those passages to the model with the question. The quality of the answers depends on the quality of the documents.

**Is it safe to connect AI to my business data?** It can be, if you control three things: which data the model can see, what it may change, and what the provider does with what you send. Give every integration the smallest access that does the job, keep write access behind an approval step, and read the provider's data and training terms.

**How much does an AI integration cost?** At Purcell Ventures, a small software project such as one integration runs $1,500 to $3,500. Full applications run $5,000 to $15,000 and up. Monthly Digital plans with ready-made AI tools run $179 to $279 a month, plus a one-time setup fee of $650 to $1,000.

**Common questions** An API is a published way for one program to read from and write to another. If your software has one, a developer can connect an AI model to it directly. If it has none, the options shrink to exports, email and copy and paste.

### AI for small business, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-for-small-business

AI for small business: how to start with safe first tasks and free tools, check AI answers, write a staff AI policy and avoid the places where AI wastes money.

**What can a small business owner use AI for each day?** AI does two jobs well: it writes first drafts, and it sorts or summarizes large amounts of text. For an owner that means replies to email and reviews, website and social copy, quotes from notes, summaries of long documents and answers to the same customer questions. A person still checks each result before it goes out.

**What are three safe first tasks for AI in a small business?** The safest first tasks are writing jobs where you already know what a good answer looks like: replies to your Google reviews, a rewrite of one page of your website, and this week's update to customers. You can judge each result yourself, and nothing reaches a customer until you send it.

**How do I check whether an AI answer is accurate?** Check four things against a source you trust before an AI answer reaches a customer: names, numbers, quotes and dates. A wrong one of these does the most damage when it goes out under your business name.

**Does my small business need an AI use policy for employees?** Yes, once more than one person uses AI tools for work. A one-page policy names the approved tools, lists the information that never goes into a chat, says who checks AI output before customers see it, and states whether staff should mention AI use to customers.

**Do I have to tell customers when I use AI?** No US law requires a small business to label every AI-drafted email or post. Laws against deceptive advertising still apply to what the text claims, and some states require a bot to identify itself in certain sales conversations. A chatbot on your website should say it is a bot, and a reply sent under a person's name should be one that person read.

**Where does AI waste a small business's money?** AI wastes money when it attaches to a process that was already broken. An AI receptionist that books appointments into a calendar nobody checks, or captures leads nobody calls back, works as designed and still earns nothing. Fix the process first, then add the tool.

**Which AI subscriptions are worth paying for?** One paid plan of a general assistant such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini covers most of what a small team needs, and a business plan adds the admin and data controls a staff policy depends on. Pay for a specialized AI tool only after it passes the three questions above.

**Will AI replace employees at a small business?** In a small business, AI takes over tasks such as drafting and sorting, and those tasks rarely make up a whole job. The time it frees can go to customer work that needs a person. Whether it leads to fewer hires depends on how the owner uses that time.

### AI websites for small businesses, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-websites

AI websites for small businesses: how to get found in ChatGPT and Google AI answers, what schema and llms.txt do, and when an AI site builder is enough.

**How does a business show up in ChatGPT and Google AI answers?** An AI assistant describes a business from the pages it can read: your website, your Google Business Profile, directories and reviews. It shows up correctly when crawlers can reach those sources, the sources agree with each other, and state plainly what the business does, where it is and who it serves.

**How can I check what ChatGPT says about my business?** Open a private window, sign out, and ask a general question first, such as the best business of your type in your town, without naming yours. Then ask about your business by name, and then ask where the assistant got its answer. The sources it names are the pages to fix.

**What is the difference between SEO and generative engine optimization?** Search engine optimization helps a page rank in a list of links. Generative engine optimization helps an AI assistant pick a sentence from your page and repeat it in an answer. Most of the work overlaps, and the difference is in how the page states its facts.

**Does schema markup help AI find my business?** Schema markup is a block of data in a page's code that labels facts such as the business name, address, hours and services. It helps machines read those facts without guessing. It helps only when the same facts appear in the visible page, and it cannot rescue a page that never states them.

**What is an llms.txt file, and does my business need one?** An llms.txt file is a plain-text file at the root of a website that lists the main pages and what each one is for, written for AI systems to read. Adoption is not universal, and nobody can promise results from one. For a site with more than a few pages, it takes about twenty minutes and costs nothing.

**Should I block AI crawlers from my website?** Most local businesses should let them in. An assistant that cannot read your site describes your business from directories and reviews instead. Blocking makes sense for a business whose product is its writing or research, since that content is what the crawlers take.

**Will Google penalize my website for AI-written content?** Google has said it ranks content on whether it helps the reader, whoever or whatever wrote it. Its spam policies target pages mass-produced to rank with little value for a reader. A page that AI drafted, a person checked, and that states real facts about your business stays within those policies.

**Are AI website builders good enough for a small business?** For a simple site the owner will keep updated, an AI builder from Wix, Squarespace or a similar company is often enough. A custom site fits when you need booking, payments, integrations with your other software, or full control of the code and structured data.

### AI glossary for small business owners, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-glossary

Plain definitions of AI terms a small business owner meets, from AI agent and token to AEO, llms.txt and GPTBot, each with an example from a real business.

**A** AEO is the work of shaping web pages so answer engines quote them. It means a clear question, a direct answer in the first sentence or two, accurate facts and structured data a machine can read.

**C** A chatbot is a program that holds a text conversation. Older chatbots follow fixed scripts. Chatbots built on large language models write their own replies, which makes them flexible and also able to say wrong things.

**D** Data retention is how long an AI provider keeps your prompts, files and replies, and what it does with them in that time. It differs by provider and by plan, and business plans usually offer shorter retention or more control.

**E** An embedding turns a piece of text into a list of numbers that captures its meaning, so texts with similar meanings land close together. Software uses embeddings to find the passages that match a question even when the words differ.

**F** Fine-tuning trains an existing model further on your own examples so it adopts a style, format or task. It changes how the model responds. For answers that depend on your current facts, retrieval usually fits better and costs less.

**G** Generative AI is AI that produces new content, such as text, images, audio, video or code, from a prompt. Chat tools, image generators and voice clones all fall under it.

**H** A hallucination is a confident answer from an AI model that is false, such as an invented fact, quote, price or source. Models predict likely text and have no built-in check for truth, so a person has to verify anything that matters.

**I** Inference is the act of running a trained model to get an output. Each question you ask a chatbot is an inference, and API providers charge for inference by the token.

### AI in small business: statistics with sources
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-small-business-statistics

Statistics on AI in U.S. small businesses from the Census Bureau, the Federal Reserve, SBA, Pew and Gallup: adoption, uses, barriers, results and AI search.

**How should I read these numbers?** Read each figure against who the survey asked and what it counted as AI use. The surveys below disagree by a wide margin because they measure different things.

**How do customers use AI to search?** For what this means for a business website, see AI websites for small businesses , or run the free AI visibility check on your own site.

**Common questions** It depends on the survey. The Census Bureau put AI use at about 20% of all U.S. businesses in spring 2026, counting use in any business function in the past two weeks. The Federal Reserve's Small Business Credit Survey found 46% of employer firms with 1 to 499 employees using AI in fall 2025. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce found 58% of small businesses using generative AI in 2025.

### AI for flooring companies, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-for/flooring-companies

AI for flooring companies: estimate write-ups from measurements, quote follow-ups, showroom questions and review replies, what stays with the installer.

**What can AI do for a flooring company?** AI handles four flooring jobs well: writing estimates from the measurements your estimator takes, following up on open quotes, answering the same showroom and product questions, and drafting replies to Google reviews. Each one is writing or sorting work that repeats every week, and a person checks the result before it reaches a customer.

**How does AI write a flooring estimate from measurements?** The estimator records room dimensions, the product, the subfloor condition and any stairs or transitions. A model turns those notes into a written estimate in your format, with square footage, waste allowance, removal, prep and install as separate lines. The estimator checks each figure before the customer sees it.

**How do I follow up on flooring quotes with AI?** Keep every open quote in one list with the date sent, then send a short follow-up on fixed days until the customer answers. AI writes a message that names the room and the product the customer picked. A scheduling tool or CRM sends it, and the owner calls anyone who replies.

**Can AI answer showroom and product questions?** Yes, for the questions you already answer every week: which lines you carry, how to clean luxury vinyl, whether you install on stairs, your service area and how to book a measure. Write those answers down first, then a website chatbot or a staff member with an AI assistant can give them at any hour.

**What should a flooring company not hand to AI?** Keep measuring, subfloor and moisture calls, product recommendations for a specific room, and final pricing with your estimator and installers. A model cannot see the job site, and manufacturer warranties depend on install conditions only your crew can check. AI drafts the paperwork around those decisions.

**What privacy rules apply to flooring customer data in AI tools?** Treat customer names, addresses, phone numbers and job notes as private, and keep card numbers, lockbox codes and alarm details out of AI chats entirely. Use a business plan of your AI tool with training on your chats turned off. This is general information, and your own counsel can answer questions about your state.

**What should a dental office not hand to AI?** Keep clinical answers, treatment plans, diagnoses and anything about a specific patient with your dentists and staff. ### AI for law firms, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/ai-for/law-firms

AI for law firms: intake screening under strict confidentiality limits and first drafts an attorney reviews, and why a bot never gives legal advice.

**What can AI do for a small law firm?** AI handles three jobs well in a small firm: screening website and phone inquiries before an attorney calls back, writing first drafts of routine letters and documents, and summarizing long records. Each one saves attorney and staff time, and an attorney reviews every result before it reaches a client, a court or the other side.

**How can AI screen legal intake inquiries?** A website chat or intake form can collect a name, contact details, the practice area, the names of the other parties and any deadline, then route the inquiry to the right attorney. It tells the visitor that no attorney-client relationship exists yet and asks them to hold back confidential details until someone from the firm calls.

**Can AI draft legal documents for attorney review?** Yes, as a starting point. A model can draft an engagement letter from your template, a demand letter from the facts you give it, or a summary of a deposition or a medical record. The attorney rewrites, checks every fact against the file, and signs the final version as their own work.

**Why should a law firm chatbot never give legal advice?** A chatbot that answers "do I have a case" or "what should I do" gives legal advice with no attorney behind it, and a visitor may rely on it. A firm's bot answers questions about the firm itself, such as practice areas, office hours and how consultations work, and sends every legal question to an attorney.

**What should a law firm not hand to AI?** Keep legal judgment, client advice, conflicts decisions, deadlines and anything filed with a court with attorneys and staff. A model cannot weigh a client's goals or the local judge, and it states wrong law in the same confident tone as right law. Use it for drafts and summaries only.

**What confidentiality limits apply to AI in a law firm?** A lawyer's duty of confidentiality covers client information typed into an AI tool, and the duty of competence covers knowing how that tool stores and uses it. The American Bar Association addressed generative AI in Formal Opinion 512 in July 2024, and several state bars have issued their own guidance. This is general information, and your own bar's rules and ethics counsel govern your firm.

**What can Purcell Ventures set up for a law firm?** I can train your attorneys and staff, add intake and FAQ tools to your website, or build a small tool around your own templates. Each route has a published price on its own page, and the first conversation about which one fits is free.

**Common questions** Only within the firm's ethics duties on confidentiality and competence. The ABA addressed generative AI in Formal Opinion 512, and several state bars have issued their own guidance. Use a business plan with training on your data turned off, keep client confidences out of any tool the firm has not approved, and have an attorney review every output.

AI copy can slip in steering words such as "perfect for young families," so a person reads every line. This is general information, and your broker or a lawyer can answer questions about a specific listing.

### AI for churches, Purcell Ventures

A model has no calling, no relationship with your members and no accountability to your elders, and it will still answer questions about faith with confidence. AI for accountants and tax preparers: document intake checklists, engagement letter drafts and tax-season FAQs, with strict limits on client financial data.

Each job repeats every season, and none of them needs AI to see a client's return.

**How does AI help with client document intake?** AI can draft a checklist for each client type, such as a salaried household, a sole proprietor, a rental property owner or a small partnership, and write the first request email and two follow-ups in your firm's voice.

**Can AI draft engagement letters and client emails?** Yes, as first drafts. **Can AI answer tax-season questions for clients?** For questions about your firm, yes. **What should an accounting firm not hand to AI?** Keep tax positions, return review, signatures and anything about a specific client's finances with your preparers. A model will quote a deduction limit or a filing rule in a confident tone, and it can be a year out of date or simply wrong.

**What confidentiality rules apply to AI in an accounting firm?** Tax preparers work under federal rules on taxpayer data. Section 7216 of the Internal Revenue Code limits how a preparer may use or disclose return information, and the IRS expects professional preparers to keep a written information security plan, as its Publication 4557 explains. CPAs also answer to their own professional and state board rules. This is general information, and your counsel or professional body can confirm what applies to your firm.

AI for insurance agents: quote request intake, renewal reminders and policy FAQs, and why a bot never binds coverage or tells a client what coverage to buy.

A model will tell a caller in a confident tone that the policy covers a flood, and that answer can leave a family uninsured and your agency facing a complaint.

### Custom AI agent vs Zapier for a small business
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/custom-ai-agent-vs-zapier

Custom AI agent vs Zapier for a small business: when a Zapier workflow is enough and when an agent pays off, plus how each charges and who maintains it.

**When is Zapier the right call?** Zapier is the right call when you can state the job as one rule: when this happens, do that. A new form entry becomes a row in your CRM and a welcome email. A paid invoice sends a thank-you note. A new booking sends a text reminder the day before.

**When does a custom AI agent make sense?** A custom agent earns its fee when the job needs reading and judgment that a fixed rule cannot express. Five signs point that way:

**What goes wrong with each one?** Zapier workflows fail without warning when an app changes a field name or a login expires. The Zap stops, and nobody notices until a customer asks why they never heard back. Turn on error emails and check the task history once a week.

**What does each one cost?** Zapier has a free plan and paid plans that charge by the number of tasks your workflows run each month, with more features on the higher plans. Each action a workflow performs counts as a task, so a busy workflow costs more than a quiet one. Prices change, so check current pricing on Zapier's site before you compare.

**Can you use both?** Yes, and it is often the cheapest path. Zapier can send data to a web address with a webhook step, so a custom agent can handle the one step that needs judgment while Zapier keeps moving data between your other apps. You pay a developer for the hard step and keep the easy ones in a tool you can edit.

**What should you ask before you pay for either?** The AI cost calculator turns the first answer into hours and dollars. The AI automation guide covers which task to automate first.

**Common questions** Zapier started as a tool that runs fixed steps when something happens in another app. It now sells AI steps and an agent product of its own, so the line keeps moving. A custom agent differs in who writes it: a developer builds it around your process, your data and your limits.

**How do I get in touch?** Email elijah@purcellventures.co or call (205) 462-7839 with the job you want to automate. If Zapier will do it, I will say so. I reply within one business day.

### AI website builder vs a custom site, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/ai-website-builder-vs-custom-site

AI website builder vs custom site for a small business: when a builder is enough and when a custom site is worth the build fee. Covers cost and what you own.

**What does an AI website builder do?** Wix, Squarespace and several other companies now ask you a few questions about your business and draft a whole site from the answers: pages, text, images and a color scheme. You edit the draft in a visual editor and publish it on their hosting. You pay a subscription for as long as the site stays up.

**When is a builder the right call?** A builder is the better buy in four common cases:

**When is a custom site worth the build fee?** A custom site pays off when the website has to do work, beyond describing the business. Five signs point that way:

**Which one do AI assistants read better?** AI assistants describe a business from the text and structured data they can read. Some builders send that text in the page itself, and some draw it with JavaScript after the page loads, which leaves a crawler that skips scripts with an almost empty page. A custom site lets the developer choose server-rendered pages and write the business markup by hand.

**What does each one cost over three years?** A builder costs a subscription every month for as long as the site exists, and the plans with booking or online sales cost more than the basic ones. Prices change, so check current pricing on the builder's site and multiply the monthly figure by 36.

**What do you own if you leave?** This question matters more than the price. With a builder, your pages live in the builder's format, and how much you can export depends on the company. Your domain is yours only if you registered it in your own name.

**Common questions** For a simple site that the owner will keep up to date, often yes. Check that the builder lets you edit page titles and descriptions, connect your own domain and export your content before you commit.

### ChatGPT vs Claude for a small business, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/chatgpt-vs-claude-for-small-business

ChatGPT vs Claude for a small business: plan structure, team data controls, the features that differ, and how to test both on your own work before you buy.

**Which one writes better?** Both write drafts good enough for emails, review replies, proposals and website copy, and the gap between them shifts with each model release. A ranking from six months ago may already be out of date, so test them on your own work.

**Is the free plan enough?** For one owner trying AI on a few tasks a week, often yes. Both free plans limit how much you can use them and which models you get. Upgrade when you hit those limits more than once a week.

**When does a team plan make sense?** Once two or three people use an assistant every week, move them to a team plan. Team plans on both products add central billing, admin controls and the business data terms described in the table. Those controls make a staff AI policy enforceable. The AI for small business guide covers writing that policy.

**What about building your own tools on them?** Both companies sell API access that developers use to build AI into your own software, billed by usage. The chat subscription and the API are separate purchases. The free AI tools on this site run on the Claude API. When I wrote about my CRM in May 2026, its AI features had cost $15 in API usage. The custom AI agent vs Zapier comparison covers when a build is worth it.

**What does training your team cost?** At Purcell Ventures, 1-on-1 sessions cost $175 an hour, small groups of 2 to 8 cost $125 a person, and a half-day workshop for up to 20 people costs $2,500. Bring examples of your own work to the session. The consulting page lists the sessions, and the AI readiness test shows where your team stands in three minutes.

**Common questions** Neither wins for every business, and the answer shifts with each model release. Run the same three tasks from your own week through both free plans and pick the one whose drafts need the least editing.

### AI consultant vs agency vs freelancer, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/ai-consultant-vs-agency-vs-freelancer

Who to hire for AI work: an independent AI consultant, an agency, a marketplace freelancer or doing it yourself. When each one fits and how each one charges.

**When should you do it yourself?** Do it yourself when the job is learning a chat assistant. Drafting emails, summarizing documents, writing first drafts of posts and researching a question all fit in a paid ChatGPT or Claude plan and a few weeks of practice. Nobody needs to build anything.

**When is a marketplace freelancer the right call?** A freelancer from a marketplace fits a single task you can describe on one page. A script that moves data from one spreadsheet into another, a chatbot set up on a platform you already chose, or a prompt library for one job. The marketplace shows past reviews and holds the payment until you approve the work.

**When is an agency worth it?** An agency earns its fee on a large project that needs several skills at the same time. A rebuild that touches design, a mobile app, a data system and a marketing launch fits that shape. An agency can staff each part, keep the work moving when one person is out, and sign a contract with terms your legal team expects.

**When does an independent consultant fit?** An independent consultant fits the middle: work too custom for a marketplace listing and too small for an agency minimum. The same person scopes the job, builds it and answers the phone when it breaks, so nothing gets lost between a salesperson and an engineer.

**What does each one cost?** Agencies usually charge a project fee or a monthly retainer, and many set a minimum engagement. Marketplace freelancers charge hourly or a fixed price per job, and some marketplaces add a client fee on top. Rates vary widely in both groups, so get a written quote and check current pricing with each one.

**What should you ask before you hire anyone?** The AI cost calculator shows how many hours a job costs your team now, which tells you how much any of these options can be worth.

**Common questions** An independent consultant is one person who scopes, builds and supports the work. An agency is a team with separate people for sales, project management, design and engineering. The agency can run more work at once, and the consultant puts the person who scoped the job on the build.

**How do I get in touch?** Email elijah@purcellventures.co or call (205) 462-7839 with the job you have in mind. If a freelancer, an agency or your own team fits it better, I will say so. I reply within one business day.

### Hire an AI consultant or do it yourself, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/hire-ai-consultant-vs-do-it-yourself

Should a small business learn AI tools itself or pay for help? When doing it yourself is enough, when a consultant pays back, and what each one costs you.

**When is doing it yourself enough?** Doing it yourself is enough when one person wants help with writing and thinking. Drafting emails and quotes, turning notes into a clean summary, writing a first pass at a job post and researching a supplier all work in a paid chat assistant. Use it on real work every day for two or three weeks and you will know what it does well and where it makes things up.

**When does paying for help save money?** Paying for help saves money when a mistake costs more than the help. Four kinds of jobs fit that test:

**How do you tell which side you are on?** Take the free AI readiness test . Ten questions score your team out of 30 and give you three next steps, with no email required. A low score on data rules points toward help. A high score on daily use points toward doing it yourself.

**What does each path cost?** Doing it yourself costs a chat assistant plan for each person who uses it, plus the hours spent learning. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini each offer a free plan and paid plans per user, with business plans that add admin and data controls. Prices change, so check current pricing on each company's site.

**What goes wrong with each path?** Doing it yourself goes wrong in two quiet ways. Someone pastes customer details into a free plan whose data terms nobody read, or someone sends an AI draft with a wrong fact because it sounded sure of itself. Both are easy to prevent with a one-page rule sheet and a habit of checking every number and name.

**Can you do both?** Yes, and it is the path I recommend most often. Learn the chat assistant on your own for a few weeks, write down where you got stuck, then book a short session on those exact problems. You pay for two hours instead of ten, and the session answers questions you already have.

**Common questions** Yes. Most owners can learn to draft, summarize and research with a paid chat assistant in a few weeks of regular use. The free tutorials and glossary on this site cover the basics. Paid help speeds up the learning and matters most when a whole team needs the same habits.

**How do I get in touch?** Email elijah@purcellventures.co or call (205) 462-7839 with what you have tried so far. If you can finish it on your own, I will say so. I reply within one business day.

### AI chatbot vs a human receptionist, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/compare/ai-chatbot-vs-human-receptionist

AI chatbot or phone answering vs a human receptionist: what software handles well, what a person must handle, and how each one charges a small business.

**What does a website chatbot handle well?** A website chatbot answers the questions customers ask over and over. What time do you open on Saturday? Do you take walk-ins? How much is a standard cleaning? Where do I park? Trained on your own answers, a chatbot gives the same reply at 11 p.m. that you would give at noon, and it can send the customer to your booking page.

**What can AI phone answering do?** AI voice tools can answer a call, give hours and prices, take a message and book into a connected calendar. They do well on short, predictable calls. They handle a caller with an unusual problem poorly, and an upset caller worse.

**What must a person handle?** A person should handle any conversation where the right answer depends on judgment, feelings or money:

**How does each one charge?** Website chatbots come as monthly plans from chatbot companies, as a feature inside a website or CRM plan, or as a custom build with a fee up front and model usage after. AI phone answering services usually charge a monthly plan with a set number of minutes or calls, or a rate per minute. A receptionist costs an hourly wage plus payroll costs, and a live answering service charges by minutes or calls. Prices change, so check current pricing with each provider.

**Which one should you choose?** Start with the question your customers ask most and where they ask it. If most of them visit your website first and ask the same few things, a chatbot and an online booking page cover a lot of ground. If most of them call, and the calls are short and routine, an AI phone tool with a transfer to a person may help. If the calls are long, personal or emotional, keep a receptionist, and give them a booking page so they spend less time on scheduling.

**Common questions** For routine questions on your website, such as hours, prices, services and how to book, a chatbot can answer at any hour. It cannot calm an upset customer, make an exception or notice that something feels wrong. Most small businesses that use one keep a person for everything outside the routine.

**How do I get in touch?** Email elijah@purcellventures.co or call (205) 462-7839 with the questions your customers ask most. If a chatbot will not help, I will say so. I reply within one business day.

## Research

### Research on small business websites, Purcell Ventures
URL: https://purcellventures.co/research

Purcell Ventures research on small business websites: measured checks of working pages, structured data, AI crawler rules, llms.txt and speed, with the data.

**How the studies work** Every study starts from public data. The Alabama study drew its business listings from OpenStreetMap through the public Overpass API, kept 2,102 unique business domains after dropping chains, government offices, schools and nonprofits, and drew its statewide sample at random with a fixed seed, so anyone can repeat the draw.

### Alabama small business websites in 2026, 700 sites checked
URL: https://purcellventures.co/research/alabama-small-business-websites-2026

I checked 700 Alabama small business websites in November 2026. 15.4% had no working home page and 16.7% had all three AI search signals I tested.

**What did the check find?** The statewide figures come from a random draw of 700 of the 2,102 business domains that OpenStreetMap lists for Alabama. The city figures cover every listed domain inside each city limit. Percentages for page checks use the 552 pages that stayed on the business's own domain as the base.

**How do the five cities compare?** Each bar shows one city's share, with the statewide sample in grey for reference. The n under each name is the base for that bar. Montgomery and Tuscaloosa have small bases, so a single site moves their figures by two to three points.

**Full results by check** Each table lists the count, the share and the base n for the statewide sample and the five cities. Download every figure as a CSV file . It holds counts, bases and percentages only.

**Method** Business listings came from OpenStreetMap through the public Overpass API at overpass-api.de on 9 November 2026. The statewide query ran at 22:05 UTC and the five city queries between 22:19 and 22:31 UTC. The query asks for every Alabama listing tagged shop, craft or office, every restaurant, cafe, bar, fast food outlet, dentist, doctor's office, clinic and veterinarian, every hotel and every fitness centre, where the listing has a website or contact:website tag.

**Common questions** It checked the home page of each business website for a working response, https, a viewport tag, a title, a meta description and Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD. It also read robots.txt for five AI crawlers, looked for an llms.txt file and timed the first byte and the HTML download from one computer in Tuscaloosa.

**Data credit and license** Listing data © OpenStreetMap contributors , available under the Open Database License. The aggregate figures on this page and in the CSV carry a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license. Credit Purcell Ventures and OpenStreetMap contributors when you use them.

## Blog

### What happens when your business domain lapses
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/business-domain-lapse-renewal

When a domain registration expires, your site and email stop working and the name can go back on sale. Here is how to keep yours renewed.

**What happens on the expiration date** When a registration expires, the registrar usually points the domain to a parking page, so customers who type your address see an ad page or a notice in place of your site. Email sent to addresses on that domain stops arriving.

**Who can buy it next** Once those periods end, the registry releases the name, and anyone can register it. Some registrars also auction expiring domains before release.

**Find out who your registrar is and when the domain expires** Go to lookup.icann.org and type your domain. The result shows the registrar's name and the expiration date. Write both down.

**Four settings that keep it renewed** Turn on auto renew in the registrar's dashboard. With auto renew on, the registrar charges the card on file before the expiration date.

**Lock the domain while you are in the account** Most registrars offer a setting called registrar lock or transfer lock. It blocks anyone from moving the domain to another registrar without first unlocking it from your account. Turn it on and leave it on unless you plan a transfer.

**Questions** Type your domain at lookup.icann.org. The result lists the expiration date and the registrar.

### Four parts of a prompt that gets a usable answer
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/prompt-usable-answer-first-time

The reader, the goal, an example and the limits: a four part prompt for local business writing, with a full example for a salon.

**Name who the work is for** An AI tool knows nothing about your customers unless you describe them. Ask it for a post about your bakery's new hours and it has to guess who will read it.

**Say what you want** State the task, the format and the length. The request "write something about our hours" leaves the format and length open. The request "write a Facebook post of three sentences announcing that we now open at 7 AM on Saturdays" states the platform, the length and the news.

**Show an example** Paste one piece of writing you already like, such as an old post, an email you sent a customer or a paragraph from your website. Then add: "Match the tone and length of this example."

**Set the limits** Limits are the rules the answer has to follow. For a small business, common limits include a word count, no prices, no emojis, no promised delivery times and no mention of a competitor.

**A full prompt for a real task** Here is a prompt a salon owner could send to announce a holiday closure:

**Fix a weak answer by fixing the prompt** When an answer misses, look at which of the four parts it got wrong. A post that sounds stiff usually needs a better example. A post that runs long needs a word count in the limits. A post with a made up detail needs the real fact typed into the prompt.

**Check the answer** Before you send what the AI wrote, compare every date, name, price and link with your own records. Models can state wrong things confidently, and your customers will read the email as coming from you.

**Questions** Only if you type them into the prompt, or the tool searches a source that lists them. Type them in to be safe.

### Who controls your domain, hosting and website login
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/who-controls-your-domain-hosting-and-login

How a local business owner can find out who holds the domain, hosting and site login today, and how to move all three into the owner's own name.

**Find your domain registrar** Your domain is the address customers type, such as yourshop.com. You rent it from a company called a registrar, such as GoDaddy, Namecheap, Squarespace or Cloudflare.

**Find your hosting company** Hosting is the server that stores your site's files and sends them to visitors. The name servers from the ICANN lookup show where your domain's settings live, and they often point to the hosting company. Names that include wixdns, squarespacedns or a host's brand name the company directly.

**Find who holds the site login** The site login is the account you use to edit pages. For WordPress, the login page usually sits at your domain followed by /wp-admin. For Wix and Squarespace, it is the account on the builder's own website.

**Why each account belongs in your name** The person who holds the domain account controls where your address points and whether it renews. If a renewal fails because the card on file expired or the reminder went to a former employee, the domain can lapse, and after the registrar's grace period anyone can register it.

**Move the accounts into your name** Create one business email address you will keep for years, such as one on your own domain or a dedicated Gmail account. Use it for the registrar, the host and the site login.

**Questions** Type your domain into lookup.icann.org. The result shows the registrar, the expiration date and the name servers. The owner's contact details often show as redacted for privacy.

### Business site slow on a phone? Causes and free tests
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/slow-site-on-phone-causes-free-tests

The three usual reasons a small business site loads slowly on a phone, oversized photos, extra plugins and slow hosting, and the free tools that measure it.

**Measure your site with PageSpeed Insights** Google offers a free tool called PageSpeed Insights at pagespeed.web.dev. Paste in your home page address and press Analyze. The report opens on the Mobile tab, which is the one that matters for customers on phones.

**Cause one: photos far larger than the screen** A photo straight from a modern phone camera can be several megabytes and thousands of pixels wide. A phone screen shows it at a few hundred pixels wide. When a site serves the full file, every visitor downloads data they never see.

**Cause two: plugins and add-ons that load on every page** Each plugin, chat widget, social feed or slideshow can add its own scripts and styles. Many of them load on every page, including pages that never use them. A site with a long list of plugins makes a phone download and run all of that code before the page settles.

**Cause three: hosting that responds slowly** Before a page can load, your hosting server has to answer the request. On a crowded shared hosting plan, that first answer can take a long time no matter how small your photos are.

**Fix in this order** Start with photos, because resizing them takes no technical skill and often makes the largest change. Move to plugins next, testing after each change. Look at hosting last, since it may involve a new plan or a move.

**Questions** Paste your page address into PageSpeed Insights at pagespeed.web.dev and read the Mobile tab. WebPageTest at webpagetest.org is another free option that shows how each file loads.

### Why AI needs your business facts before it writes
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/tell-ai-about-your-business

What a language model can know about a local business, what it has to guess, and the one-page brief that supplies the facts.

**What the model knows and what it lacks** A language model learns from a large body of text collected up to a cutoff date. After that date, it learns nothing new on its own. If your business had public web pages before the cutoff, the model may have picked up pieces of them, and it has no way to know what you changed since.

**Write a one-page business brief** Put your facts in a short document, a business brief. Write it once, keep it in a file on your computer, and paste it at the top of any chat about your business.

**Tell it the goal for each task** The brief covers the business. Each request still needs its own instructions.

**Save the brief where the tool can reuse it** Some AI tools let you store background information so you do not have to paste it every time. Claude offers Projects, where you can add documents and instructions that apply to every chat inside that project. ChatGPT offers custom instructions that apply across your chats.

**Leave private details out of the brief** A brief should hold facts you would put on your website. Keep passwords, bank details, customer names and customer records out of it unless your business has approved the tool and its settings for that data.

**Questions** Some tools can search the web, and they still miss details you never published, such as deposit rules or a new price you have not posted yet.

### Three ways to work with AI: automation, augmentation and agency
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/automation-augmentation-agency-explained

What automation, augmentation and agency mean in Anthropic's AI Fluency framework, with one small business example for each.

**Automation for routine tasks** In automation, AI carries out defined instructions. You know exactly what you want, you spell it out, and the tool does it. You do the planning before you send the prompt.

**Augmentation for decisions** In augmentation, a person and AI think together. You start without a finished answer and work toward one over several turns of conversation.

**Agency for repeated work** In agency, a person sets AI up to do future tasks on their behalf. You do the setup once, and the AI handles each new case as it comes.

**How to pick the right mode for a task** Start with automation. Pick one task you repeat every week that follows the same steps, such as formatting a menu update or summarizing job notes. Because you already know the right answer, a mistake in the output is easy to spot and cheap to fix.

**The checks that apply in every mode** Models can state wrong things confidently, so every name, number, date and quote in an output needs a check against a source before you use it. A model also knows only its training data up to a cutoff date plus what you give it, so supply your current prices, hours and policies in the prompt.

**Questions** Anthropic teaches the AI Fluency framework in its Anthropic Academy courses. Professors Rick Dakan and Joseph Feller developed it with Anthropic.

### What a contact page needs so customers reach you on the first try
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/contact-page-that-reaches-you

The four parts of a local business contact page that let customers reach you on the first try, and how to test each one from your own phone.

**Make the phone number a tap-to-call link** On a phone, a tap-to-call link opens the dialer with your number already filled in. The customer taps once and the call starts. Without the link, they have to memorize the number or copy it by hand.

**Write your hours as text and keep them current** Put your hours on the page in plain text, one line per day or one line per group of days. Text hours load fast, read well on a small screen and stay easy to edit.

**Give the full address and a map link** Write out the street address, suite number, city, state and ZIP code. Link the address to Google Maps so a tap on a phone opens directions. If your entrance is around the back or parking is limited, add one sentence that says where to park and which door to use.

**Use one form that reaches a person** Keep the form short: name, a phone number or email, and a message box. Each extra field gives a customer one more reason to stop before they press send.

**Run the whole check from your phone** The full check takes about five minutes. Open the contact page on your phone over cell data. Tap the phone number and confirm the dialer opens. Read the hours and compare them with your Google Business Profile. Tap the address and confirm the map shows your front door. Send a test message through the form and find it in your inbox.

**Questions** A tap-to-call link wraps your phone number in a tel: link, so tapping the number on a phone opens the dialer with the number filled in. Without it, a customer has to type or copy the number by hand.

### AI social media posts: what to hand off, what to write
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/ai-social-media-posts-what-to-hand-off

Which social media jobs a small business can give to an AI tool, which posts the owner should write, and how to check every draft before it goes up.

**Decide which jobs AI should draft** AI Fluency starts with Delegation, which means deciding whether, when and how AI should take part in a task. For social media, I sort the work with one question: does this post need facts or feelings that only you can supply?

**Put your facts in the prompt** A model knows only its training data up to a cutoff date, plus whatever you type into the chat. It has no record of your hours, your menu, this weekend's special or the name of your new stylist. If you leave those out, the tool fills the space with general wording or with details that sound right and turn out wrong.

**Write these posts yourself** Some posts should come from you from the first word. A reply to an unhappy customer is one of them. That person wants to hear from the owner, and a polished paragraph from a chat tool can sound like a form letter at the worst moment.

**Check every draft before you publish it** Discernment is the AI Fluency term for judging how useful an output actually is. Models can state wrong things confidently, so I check every name, number and date in a draft against a source before I use it. For a business post, that source is your own calendar, price list or menu.

**Keep customer details out of the chat window** The last of the 4Ds is Diligence, which means owning responsibility for how you use AI and what you do with its output. A post goes out under your business name, so you answer for it whether you or a tool wrote the first draft.

**Questions** An AI tool can draft most routine captions from your notes. Write replies to unhappy customers, posts about specific people and the story of your business yourself, and check every draft for names, dates and prices before you publish it.

### How to check an AI answer before you use it
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/check-ai-answer-before-using

A routine for checking the names, numbers, quotes and dates in an AI answer against a source before they reach customers.

**Why a confident answer can still be wrong** A language model writes the words most likely to come next, based on its training data. That process produces fluent sentences, and fluency says nothing about accuracy. A model can give you a wrong phone number for a supplier in the same tone it uses to give you a correct one.

**Names** Check every person, business, product and place the answer names. Search each name and confirm it exists with the same spelling the answer uses.

**Numbers** Treat every number as a claim that needs a source. That includes prices, tax rates, measurements, phone numbers, addresses and counts.

**Quotes** AI models sometimes produce quotes that sound right and that nobody ever said. Before you use a quote, find it in its original place: the book, the speech, the interview or the article.

**Dates** Dates go wrong in two ways. The answer can give a wrong date for a past event, and it can treat old information as current because of its training cutoff.

**A routine you can repeat** Print or copy the AI answer and highlight every name, number, quote and date. Check each highlighted item against a source and write the source next to it. Anything without a source gets cut or rewritten.

**Questions** You can, and it sometimes catches errors, but its second answer comes from the same model. Confirm facts against an outside source.

### Fix your Google Business Profile before you pay for website work
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/google-business-profile-before-website

Your Google Business Profile can show your hours, phone and address right on the search page. Here are the fields to check first, at no cost.

**Find and claim your profile** Search for your business name and city on Google. If a panel for your business appears, look for a link that says Own this business or Claim this business. If you already manage it, sign in at business.google.com with the Google account you used to claim it.

**Hours, including holiday hours** Check the regular hours for every day of the week against the sign on your door. Then open the section for special hours and enter each holiday closure before the holiday arrives.

**Phone number and website link** Call the phone number on your profile from another phone. It should ring a line that someone answers during business hours. Watch for an old number from a previous location or a personal cell phone nobody checks anymore.

**Business name and category** Type your business name exactly as it appears on your sign and your receipts. Google's guidelines tell owners to leave out extra keywords and city names, and a name stuffed with keywords can lead Google to suspend the profile.

**Address or service area** If customers come to you, enter the street address and move the map pin onto your actual entrance. In a shopping center, the default pin can land on the wrong side of the building.

**Why the profile comes first** Your website only reaches people who click through to it. The profile can appear for people who search your name, people who search for your kind of business nearby and people who browse Google Maps. Once the hours, phone number and address on the profile are right, make sure your website shows the same ones, so a customer gets the same answer in both places.

**Questions** No. Claiming and editing a profile at business.google.com is free.

### A quick phone test for your business website
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/quick-phone-test-business-website

Five checks to run on your own phone, from sideways scrolling to a tappable phone number, plus a way to preview other phone sizes in Chrome.

**Step one: open the site as a customer** Log out of your website's editor first, so you see the public page. Open your phone's browser, type your web address and wait for the page to load. Hold the phone upright.

**Step two: drag the page sideways** Put your thumb on the middle of the page and drag left. If the whole page slides and you see a blank strip or cut off text on the right, something on the page is wider than the screen.

**Step three: read a paragraph without zooming** Pick your menu or your list of services and try to read it at normal size. If you have to pinch and zoom, the page is showing the desktop layout shrunk down to phone width.

**Step four: tap every link with your thumb** Tap each item in your menu with your thumb. If you hit the wrong link, the links are too small or too close together. Ask your web person to add space around each button and link.

**Step five: find your hours from the home page** Go back to the home page and look for your hours without opening the menu. If they only appear on a separate page, a customer has to tap through the menu to find them.

**A second look from your computer** To see your site at several phone sizes, open it in Google Chrome on a computer, right click the page and choose Inspect. In the panel that opens, click the icon that shows a phone and a tablet. Chrome redraws the page at phone width, and the menu at the top lets you pick different phone models.

**Questions** No. Your own phone covers the main checks, and Google Chrome on a computer can preview other phone sizes for free.

### What to keep out of an AI chat window when you run a business
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/keep-out-of-ai-chat-window

Passwords, customer records and private details do not belong in an AI chat, and placeholders get you the same help without them.

**Where your text goes** When you type into a chat tool, the tool sends your text to the company that runs it. Depending on the tool and your plan, that company may store the conversation and may use it to train future models.

**Passwords and login codes** Never paste a password, a two-factor code or a recovery key into a chat. That covers the login for your website host, your domain registrar, your bank and your email. An AI tool needs none of them to help you.

**Customer records and payment details** Customer names, phone numbers, home addresses, card numbers and order histories are private to your customers. Keep them inside the systems where you already store them, such as your point of sale and your email.

**Private details about you and your staff** Leave out Social Security numbers, tax IDs, bank account numbers, employee pay, health information and anything from a personnel file. A question about payroll software works fine with invented numbers.

**What you can paste freely** Your public menu, your posted hours, the text on your website, a product description and a job listing you plan to publish are all fine to paste. So is a rough draft of a social media post or a question about how to word a refund policy.

**A written rule for your team** Pick one AI tool for the business and note which plan you pay for. Open its privacy settings and decide whether chats may go toward training. Then write a three-line note for everyone who uses it: no passwords, no customer details, use placeholders. Pin it in your team chat or tape it next to the register.

**Questions** Most AI companies publish a privacy policy and a page on how they use chats. Search the tool's name plus privacy policy, and read the section on training.

### Start using AI in your business: three safe first tasks
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/start-using-ai-this-week-three-safe-first-tasks

Three low-risk ways a small business owner can start using AI this week, plus the checks to run on every answer before a customer sees it.

**Setting up your account before you type anything** Pick one tool. ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini all have free plans that can handle these tasks. Sign up with your business email so your work stays separate from your personal chats.

**Choosing tasks you can check yourself** First decide whether AI should do the task at all. For a first week, I pick tasks where you can spot a wrong answer quickly, a mistake costs little to fix, and the work takes time you would rather spend with customers.

**Task one: drafting replies to your Google reviews** Open your Google Business Profile, go to Reviews, and copy the text of one review. Paste it into the AI tool with a prompt like this: "Write a short, friendly reply to this review for my barbecue restaurant in Tuscaloosa. Thank the customer, mention the dish they named, and keep it under four sentences. Do not offer discounts or refunds."

**Task two: rewriting one page of your website** Pick the page you like least, often the services page or the about page, and copy its text into the tool. This task works best as a back-and-forth where you and the tool work on the page together.

**Task three: writing this week's customer update** Pick one piece of news, such as your Thanksgiving hours or a new service. Write the facts yourself first: dates, times, address and phone number.

**How to check every result before you use it** Models can state wrong things with full confidence, so I check every fact, name, number and quote against a source before I use it.

### "Not secure" next to your website: what it means and the fix
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/not-secure-label-website-fix

Why Chrome shows "Not secure" next to your business web address, and the steps to fix it on a typical small business host this week.

**What the label tells your visitors** Every website address starts with either http or https. The s at the end stands for secure. When a site uses https, the browser and your web server encrypt the information that passes between them. Someone on the same coffee shop Wi-Fi cannot read it.

**Why browsers show it on a site that sells nothing** Owners often tell me their site has no checkout, so the warning should not matter. The browser has no way to know what your site sells. It shows the same label on a church homepage that it shows on a payment page.

**What fixing it involves** The fix has three parts. First, your site needs an SSL certificate. That is a small file on your web server that proves your site belongs to your domain and lets the browser use https.

**Doing it on a cPanel host** Many budget hosts give you a control panel called cPanel. Log in to your hosting account and open it.

**WordPress and mixed content** If your site runs on WordPress, log in and go to Settings, then General. Change both the WordPress Address (URL) and Site Address (URL) fields so they start with https. Click Save Changes. You may need to log in again afterward.

**What to check this week** Open your site in Chrome on your phone and on a computer. Look at the address bar on your homepage, your contact page and any page with a form.

### I built agents that cannot fix what they find
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/agents-that-cannot-fix-what-they-find

I split the AI agent that finds problems from the one that fixes them. That kept agents out of files they should not read and left every finding open.

**Agents get text and no tools** The first version of my reasoning layer passed the model a prompt describing exactly what it was allowed to look at. The prompt described the scope accurately, and nothing enforced it.

**The failure this design caused** If the agent that finds a problem cannot fix it, a person has to, and the system needs a way to record the fix. I built the finding half carefully and never built the closing half.

**When a finding counts as resolved** A finding is now resolved when a later audit looks for it and cannot reproduce it.

**What these failures had in common** Each of these failures returned an empty result without raising an error, and each empty result looked like good news. A ledger with nothing resolved looks like a quiet week, and a scan that returns zero rows looks like a clean one.

**Related reading** Part of the guide AI automation for small businesses .

### A shipped site can still fail to take a payment
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/shipped-is-not-activated

A site can be live with every deploy check passing and still fail to take a payment. Usually one path is broken, and the owner never sees it.

**Common small failures** Most launched sites fail that question in small ways. A payment link still carries a placeholder token from testing, so it loads and looks finished but takes no money. A pricing page lists tiers with no way to select one. A form collects an email and promises a follow-up that never got automated.

**Why nobody catches it** The person who built the site tests that each page loads. Few owners test that a stranger can complete a purchase, because that means spending money on their own business, and that feels absurd. So nobody runs the check, and the broken path can stay broken for months.

**How to check your own site** Open your own site in a private window. Start from wherever a stranger would land, which is often a different page from the one you're proud of. Try to buy from yourself. Note where you stall.

**Related reading** Part of the guide AI automation for small businesses .

### Why I charge $19 for the AI Starter Kit
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/case-for-charging-19

Why I priced the PV AI Starter Kit at $19, what it does to how people buy, and what 200 sales would add up to.

**A low price lets me skip a sales funnel** At $497, I would need a sales funnel: a webinar, an email sequence and testimonials. I would have to build all of that before selling a single copy.

**Some $19 buyers may buy a digital services plan** Someone who has paid $19 has already bought from Purcell Ventures once, which makes a second purchase an easier decision.

**Unit economics** The content in the $19 kit took 40 hours of work. If I sell 100 copies, that is $1,900, or $47.50 for each hour of build time. If I sell 1,000 copies, that is $19,000, or $475 an hour, which is above my $175 hourly consulting rate.

**A $19 purchase carries little risk** A buyer who picks the wrong kit loses $19, which changes how people buy. At $19, the buyer is testing: let's see if this is any good. At $497, the buyer is justifying: I have to prove to myself this was worth it.

**I list every file in the kit before anyone pays** When you sell a $497 course, the customer cannot see the contents until after they pay, so the sales page has to persuade them.

**A $19 price tests my delivery pipeline** If I cannot deliver $19 of value automatically, every time, with no effort per sale, my operations are not ready for a $497 product either.

**What 200 sales would mean** If I sell 200 kits a year at $19, that is $3,800 toward the build time and 200 people who have bought from me once.

### Five workflows any small business can automate without code
URL: https://purcellventures.co/blog/five-workflows-no-code

Five automations a small business can set up without writing code, and the tools I would use for each one.

**Email follow-ups for quotes you sent and forgot** You quoted a client, they didn't respond, and now it's been eleven days and you can't remember if you followed up. Forgotten follow-ups lose sales, and you can fix it in 45 minutes with Gmail.

**New customer onboarding emails** Every time someone buys, you send the same three emails: welcome, confirmation and next steps. Most owners write these from scratch every time, when they could write them once and schedule them.

**Invoice and payment reminders** If you're sending invoices and chasing payments by hand, Stripe plus an invoicing tool can send the invoices and reminders for you. The customer gets the invoice, gets reminded at 7, 14 and 30 days, and pays by card link.

**Lead forms that notify you** If your contact form collects submissions in a database you rarely check, a lead may buy from someone else before you reply. Zapier or n8n can fix this in twenty minutes: each form submission sends you a Slack message or text, so you can call back within an hour.

**Social media posts on a schedule** Many owners write four posts in a burst, then go quiet on social media for three weeks because they don't want to log in and post by hand.

**What the five have in common** Each workflow takes a task you already do by hand and puts it on a schedule so you don't have to remember it.
